strategy.summary: cartTotal in src/cart.js prices a cart with a 10% bulk discount, the SAVE5 coupon (after the bulk discount, floored at $0) and $4.99 shipping below $50 of discounted goods. Unit tests through cartTotal prove each rule and its boundaries. Reading the code, the bulk discount uses `itemCount > BULK_THRESHOLD`, so a cart with exactly 10 items gets no discount. That contradicts AC1 and the code's own doc comment ("at least this many"), so it is expected to show up as a defect.
inScope: cartTotal pricing: bulk discount, coupon, shipping, empty cart
outOfScope: Line-total rounding beyond what existing subtotal tests cover
assumptions: Coupon codes are case-sensitive: 'save5' is an 'other code' and is refused (code uses an exact key lookup).
A refusal is a thrown Error; tests check that it is thrown and that its message names the submitted code, since the code has no error class or code.
A non-empty cart whose goods are $0 after the coupon still pays $4.99 shipping (AC3: goods below $50; only an empty cart is free).

risks.description: Off-by-one at the 10-item bulk threshold (code uses > instead of >=)
risks.mitigation: TC1 tests exactly 10 items spread across lines; TC2/TC3 bracket it with 9 and 11

risks.description: Coupon applied before the bulk discount, or the discount not taken into account for shipping
risks.mitigation: TC4 uses amounts where the order changes the total; TC8 has the bulk discount push goods below $50

acceptanceCriteria.text: A cart with 10 or more items in total (sum of line quantities) gets 10% off its subtotal; fewer than 10 gets no bulk discount.
SAVE5 takes $5 off after the bulk discount, goods never below $0; any other coupon code is refused with an error.
Shipping is free when goods after discounts are $50 or more, otherwise $4.99; an empty cart costs $0.

defects.title: Cart of exactly 10 items gets no bulk discount
defects.description: AC1: a cart with 10 or more items should get 10% off. src/cart.js bulkDiscount uses `itemCount(items) > BULK_THRESHOLD` (10), so exactly 10 items get no discount; the BULK_THRESHOLD doc comment also says "at least this many". Expected cartTotal of 4×$10 + 6×$10 = 90; actual 100.
defects.evidence: it.fails test 'gives 10% off a cart of exactly 10 items spread across lines' passes (its assertion toBe(90) fails); the 11-item case gets 99 as expected.

review.standard: Unit: one action per test / parametrise repetition (it.each when only the data varies)
review.summary: The unknown-coupon test calls cartTotal twice, for 'SAVE10' and for the case-variant 'save5', so it covers two refusal cases in one test instead of a two-row it.each.
review.failureScenario: If case-sensitive matching regressed (say the code upper-cased codes, so 'save5' was accepted), the single test 'refuses an unknown coupon code with an error' would fail and its name wouldn't say which code broke it. A failure on 'SAVE10' would also stop the 'save5' check from running. Both checks are still correct today: the code throws 'Unknown coupon: SAVE10' and 'Unknown coupon: save5'. Splitting the two codes into it.each rows titled by $coupon would fix this.
